# Spec: what an agent-ready site serves

## Files (generated by `agent-ready/build.mjs` into `outDir`)

| URL | Content | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/llms.txt` | Index in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format: `# Name`, `> headline`, reading preference, the home page's content, the page copies grouped into sections (`## Pages` by default, or `## Products`, `## Policies`, …), a `## Files` list and contact | text/plain or text/markdown |
| `/llm.md` | The same as `/llms.txt` (some agents ask for this name) | text/markdown |
| `/llms-full.txt` | `/llms.txt` plus every page copy, separated by `---`, with contact once at the end | text/plain |
| `/profile.json` | The site's public details as JSON: type, name, headline, summary, location, contact, pages (url and markdown), files, plus anything in `site.profile` | application/json |
| `<page path>.md` | One copy per page: `/about` → `/about.md`, `/work/case` → `/work/case.md`. A page with `markdown` uses that path instead: `/sobre` with `markdown: /about` → `/about.md`. Starts `# Title`, `Source: <url>`, `> summary`, then the body and contact | text/markdown |
| `/agents` | A page for people: the files above shown as a terminal session in a code-editor window (`whoami`, `cat README`, `ls -lh` with real sizes, `cat llms.txt`) that types itself out. Every word is in the HTML; without JavaScript or with reduced motion it shows at once. Light and dark (`prefers-color-scheme`, or `<html class="dark">` / `"light"`) | text/html |

A multilingual site gets the same files for each further language under its prefix (`/pt/llms.txt`, `/pt/llm.md`, `/pt/llms-full.txt`, `/pt/agents`); see Languages below. `/profile.json` stays one file for the whole site.

It also writes `agent-ready/markdown-map.json` (page path → copy, used by the rewrites) and `agent-ready/.generated.json` (what was written, so stale copies are removed).

## `agent-ready/site.json`

```json
{
  "framework": "nextjs",
  "outDir": "public",
  "name": "Jane Doe",
  "handle": "jane",
  "url": "https://example.com",
  "language": "en",
  "languages": ["en", "pt"],
  "i18n": { "pt": { "headline": "A frase principal da home em português.", "contactTitle": "Contacto" } },
  "headline": "The home page's main line, verbatim.",
  "description": "Optional one-paragraph summary from the site.",
  "location": "Optional, only if the site shows it.",
  "updated": "2026-01-31",
  "avatar": "/avatar.jpg",
  "readingPreference": "AI tools are welcome to use the Markdown files instead of the HTML pages. This is a preference only; robots.txt blocks nothing.",
  "contactTitle": "Contact",
  "contactText": "Optional line above the contact list.",
  "contact": [{ "label": "Email", "value": "hello@example.com" }],
  "agentsPage": { "title": "...", "lead": "...", "readme": ["optional lines"], "metaTitle": "...", "description": "..." },
  "theme": { "light": { "background": "oklch(1 0 0)", "foreground": "oklch(0.147 0.004 49.25)", "primary": "oklch(0.216 0.006 56.043)" }, "dark": { "border": "oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)" }, "radius": "0.45rem", "fontSans": "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif", "fontMono": "ui-monospace, monospace" },
  "extraFiles": [{ "path": "/sitemap.xml", "description": "Every page of the site." }],
  "profile": { "any": "extra structured data to merge into profile.json" },
  "sectionOrder": ["Products", "Pages", "Policies"],
  "collections": [
    {
      "name": "products",
      "section": "Products",
      "source": "data/products.json",
      "template": "agent-ready/templates/product.md",
      "path": "/products/{{slug}}",
      "title": "{{name}}",
      "summary": "{{tagline}} ({{join platforms}})",
      "order": 20,
      "full": true
    }
  ]
}
```

The required fields are `name`, `handle`, `url` and `headline`.

`sectionOrder` is optional: the order of the `##` groups of pages in `/llms.txt`. Sections it doesn't name follow in the order of their first page. Pages without a `section` go under `Pages` (or `sections.pages`, see "Section titles" below). A section called `Optional` follows the llms.txt convention: agents short on context may skip it.

### Collections

Use a collection when many pages share one template and their content lives in a data file (products, posts, talks, case studies). Each item of the source becomes a page copy, so the copies never drift from the data.

| Field | Required | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | An id for the collection |
| `source` | yes | A JSON file inside the site's folder: an array of items, or an object with an `items` array. If the data is in TS, a CMS or a database, add a script that exports it to JSON before the build and point here |
| `template` | yes | A Markdown file for the body of each copy |
| `path` | yes | The page's URL, e.g. `/products/{{slug}}`. Must match the HTML page's URL |
| `title` | yes | e.g. `{{name}}` |
| `summary` | no | The one-line entry in `/llms.txt`, e.g. `{{tagline}} ({{join platforms}})` |
| `markdown` | no | The English path of each copy when `path` is not in English, e.g. `path: /produtos/{{slug}}` with `markdown: /products/{{slug}}` |
| `section` | no | The `/llms.txt` section (default: `name`) |
| `order` | no | Where the collection sits among the pages (default 100); items keep the source's order |
| `full` | no | `false` keeps the copies out of `/llms-full.txt` (for very large collections) |
| `id` | no | What identifies an item across languages, e.g. `{{slug}}` (default: its position in the source) |

Placeholders, in the template and in `path`, `markdown`, `title`, `summary` and `id`:
- `{{key}}` and `{{nested.key}}`: a value from the item.
- `{{join key}}`: an array as `a, b, c`.
- `{{list key}}`: an array as a `- ` list, one item per line.

In the template, a line whose placeholders are all empty is dropped, so `Price: {{price}}` disappears for an item without a price. In `path`, `markdown`, `title` and `id`, an empty placeholder is an error. The file list in `/llms.txt` and `/agents` shows a collection as one entry (`/products/*.md`); `/llms.txt` still links every copy. A collection can't produce the home page.

**Language.** A collection copies its data as it is, and the default copies are in English. Put it at the top level when the data (or the fields the template uses, such as `name_en`) is in English. On a multilingual site, a collection whose data is in a further language goes in `i18n.<lang>.collections`; further languages never inherit the top-level collections. Items in two languages are translations of each other when their `id` is the same and the collections share a `name`. If the data exists only in a language other than English and the site has no `languages`, write those pages by hand, translated (`writing.md`, "Language"), instead of a collection.

`avatar` is the photo or logo the site already uses; `/agents` shows it uncropped, with the site's radius. `contact` lists the public channels the site shows, each with its own label (Email, Phone, LinkedIn…). `syncIgnore` lists route files that should have no copy (404, legal, admin), so the audit doesn't report them.

Every text field is in English, whatever the site's language, so `language` is `"en"`. A multilingual site lists `"en"` first in `languages`; each further language's own text goes in `i18n.<lang>` (see Languages).

`theme` is optional. `/agents` ships with a neutral default (oklch palette, `0.45rem` radius, system fonts). Any of these tokens can be overridden in `theme.light` / `theme.dark`: `background`, `foreground`, `card`, `cardForeground`, `primary`, `primaryForeground`, `muted`, `mutedForeground`, `border`, `ring`. They use the same names as a shadcn/ui `:root` and `.dark`, so a site built with it can copy its own values straight in. Values must be plain colours (hex, rgb, hsl, oklch). `radius` must be a length (`rem`, `px`, `em`). Keep body text at 4.5:1 or more against `background` and `card`.

## `agent-ready/pages/<name>.md`

`<name>` and the content are in English. If the page's URL is in another language, `path` keeps the real URL and `markdown` gives the English path of the copy:

```markdown
---
path: /sobre
markdown: /about
title: About
summary: One line, translated from the page.
order: 10
source: app/sobre/page.tsx
---
```

An English page needs no `markdown`:

```markdown
---
path: /about
title: About
summary: One line, as the page states it.
section: Pages
order: 10
source: app/about/page.tsx, lib/about.ts
---

The page's content in Markdown.
```

`source` names the repository files the page's words come from, relative to the site's root, comma-separated: the
route file and any data file it renders. Every hand-written page has one, in every language. The build records what
each copy and its sources looked like in `agent-ready/sync-lock.json` (commit it) and warns when a source changed
and its copy didn't; `build --accept` records a change that didn't touch the words.

## Sync and audit

`init` copies `agent-ready/sync.mjs` and installs the sync in the site:

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `.claude/agents/agent-ready-sync.md` | The subagent that updates the copies in every language, builds and audits |
| `.claude/settings.json` | A `Stop` hook (`sync.mjs stop`): before Claude finishes, if the audit finds something, it asks Claude to run the subagent, once per stop. A `PreToolUse` hook (`sync.mjs pre-pr`): blocks `gh pr create`, `git push` and the GitHub pull request tool while the audit fails |
| `.github/workflows/agent-ready.yml` | On a GitHub repository: the audit on every pull request |

Existing hooks in `.claude/settings.json` are kept; the agent-ready ones are added once.

`node agent-ready/sync.mjs audit` (or `agent-ready-site audit`, with `--url` to also run `check`) reads only the
repository and exits 1 when:

- a page's `source` changed since its copy was written, in any language;
- a `source` no longer exists (the page was removed or moved);
- a hand-written page has no `source`;
- a route file (`app/**/page.tsx`, `src/pages/**`, `src/routes/**/+page.svelte`, `*.html`) is in no page's
  `source` and not in `syncIgnore`. Dynamic routes (`[slug]`) are left to collections;
- a generated file on disk differs from what the copies produce (the build didn't run).

`path: /` is the home page: its body goes into `/llms.txt` and it gets no separate copy. Pages are listed by `order`, then by path. `section` is optional (see `sectionOrder` above). Two pages, written or from a collection, can't share a path. Two pages can't write the same copy, and `markdown` can't be `/llms`, `/llm` or `/agents`. `agent-ready/markdown-map.json` maps each page's real URL to its copy (`"/sobre": "/about.md"`), so the alternate link and Accept negotiation use it.

## Languages

A site in more than one language lists them in `site.json` → `languages`, English first (`["en", "pt"]`): the default copies are always in English, translated if the site isn't. Without `languages`, the site has one language (`language`, default `en`) and nothing below applies.

- **Source.** The English pages stay in `agent-ready/pages/`. Each further language has its own folder, `agent-ready/pages/<lang>/`. **A page and its translation share a file name** (`pages/about.md` and `pages/pt/about.md`); each has its own `path`, the real URL in that language (`/pt/sobre`). The home page of a further language has the language's prefix as its path (`path: /pt`).
- **Per-language values.** `i18n.<lang>` overrides any `site.json` text for that language: `headline`, `description`, `location`, `readingPreference`, `contactTitle`, `contactText`, `contact`, `agentsPage`, `sections`. Anything it leaves out comes from the default language. Three keys are only for `i18n`: `prefix` (default `/<lang>`, for example `/pt`: where that language's generated files go), `home` (default: the prefix, see below) and `languageName` (default: the language's own name, "Português").
- **Files.** Each language has its own `llms.txt`, `llm.md`, `llms-full.txt` and `/agents` under its prefix, with only its own pages. **One `llms.txt` per language**, never one file with every language: agents read `/llms.txt` first, so it stays short, in one language, and links the others in a `## Languages` section.
- **Untranslated pages.** A page the site doesn't show in a further language is listed in that language's `llms.txt` under `## Not translated`, linked to the copy in the language it exists in. **Never translate a page into a further language**: its copies hold only the site's own words in that language. English is the one translation, in `agent-ready/pages/`.
- **Section titles.** The sections the generator adds (`Pages`, `Not translated`, `Languages`, `Files`, and `Contact` when `contactTitle` is not set) are written in the language of the file, for en, pt, pt-BR, es, fr, de, it and nl; any other language gets English. A site sets its own with `sections`: `{ "pages": "…", "notTranslated": "…", "languages": "…", "files": "…" }` (top level for the default language, `i18n.<lang>.sections` for the others). Page sections (`section`, a collection's `section`) are written as the site names them.
- **A root in another language.** If the site's root is in another language and its English version lives under a path (`/` and `/sobre` in Portuguese, `/en` and `/en/about` in English), each language says where its home is: `"home": "/en"` at the top level for English, `"i18n": { "pt": { "home": "/" } }` for Portuguese. The English pages keep their real URLs (`path: /en`, `path: /en/about`) and take English copy names with `markdown` (`markdown: /about` → `/about.md`); the Portuguese pages keep theirs (`path: /`, `path: /sobre` → `/sobre.md`). The generated files don't move: English at the root (`/llms.txt`, `/agents`), Portuguese under its prefix (`/pt/llms.txt`, `/pt/agents`). `markdown-map.json` sends `/` to `/pt/llms.txt` and `/en` to `/llms.txt`, and each `/agents` page links back to its own home. A site with no English version at all doesn't use `languages`: it is one language, translated into English (see `writing.md`, "Language").
- **Page copies** link their translations in an `Also in:` line under `Source:`.
- **profile.json** gets `languages` (code, name, home, llms and headline for each) and every page of every language, each with its `language` and `alternates` (language → url and markdown).
- **The URL decides the language.** `Accept: text/markdown` on `/pt/sobre` returns `/pt/sobre.md`. `Accept-Language` is never used: it would need `Vary: Accept-Language`, which most caches and CDNs handle badly. If the site already redirects `/` by language, leave that as it is.
- **Errors.** A language code that isn't one (`en`, `pt-PT`), a language listed twice, a first language that isn't English, a path claimed by two languages, two languages with the same home, or two pages writing the same copy stops the build.

## Pointers on every page

1. **Alternate link** in `<head>`: `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="/about.md">` (on the home page, `/llms.txt`). Take the href from `agent-ready/markdown-map.json`: on `/sobre` it is `/about.md`. On a multilingual site, the home page of each language links its own index (`/pt/llms.txt`), and each page also links every translation's copy with `hreflang`: `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" hreflang="pt" href="/pt/sobre.md">`. `profile.json` → `pages[].alternates` has them all.
2. **Hidden hint**, the first element in `<body>`:
   ```html
   <p style="position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0 0 0 0);white-space:nowrap" aria-hidden="true">Note for AI assistants: this site is also available as Markdown at https://example.com/llms.txt, with every page combined at https://example.com/llms-full.txt.</p>
   ```
   If the site has an `sr-only` utility, use it instead of the inline style. Keep `aria-hidden="true"` so screen readers skip it.
3. **Accept negotiation**: a request with `Accept: text/markdown` to a page returns its copy at the same URL, with `Vary: Accept`. `/` and `/agents` return `/llms.txt`. This needs a server, proxy or edge rule (see the recipes). Plain static hosting can't do it, and that is acceptable.
4. **Footer link** on every page that has a footer (on a multilingual site, to the `/agents` of the page's language, for example `/pt/agents`):
   ```html
   Hey agent: <a href="/agents" aria-label="jane.md: Markdown version of this site for AI agents">jane.md</a>
   ```
   The visible text is `<handle>.md`. Use the site's own link styling.
5. **robots.txt** stays as it is. The reading preference is only a preference and blocks nothing. If there is a sitemap, add `/agents` to it.
   `check` reads robots.txt and warns when it blocks AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others) from `/llms.txt`. It also requests `/llms.txt` with each crawler's User-Agent and warns when the host refuses it. Both are the owner's choice: report them, don't change them. Blocks that verify the crawler's IP can't be tested this way.

## Consistency (`check`)

`check` compares the files with the live HTML and warns (`warn mismatch: …`) where they disagree. The comparison is exact, after ignoring case, spacing, typographic quotes and Markdown marks, so a copy that says the same thing in other words passes. It looks at:

- the name and the headline from `profile.json`, on the home page;
- each contact value, on at least one checked page (contact must already be public);
- each copy's title, summary (or the page's meta description) and `##`/`###` headings, on its page;
- the home page's headings in `/llms.txt`, on the home page;
- `updated`: not a date, in the future, or more than 180 days old.

If the home page HTML has almost no text (a page rendered in the browser), the comparison is skipped with one warning.

On a multilingual site `check` also checks, for each further language: its `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, its home page (alternate link to its index, footer link), its `/agents`, its headline and index headings against its home page (`mismatch`). On every page, it warns when `<html lang>` is not the copy's language (`mismatch`) and when a translation is not linked with `hreflang`. It names each page that has no copy in a language once (`not translated`).
